newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - OMV surges as H1 earnings double.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - OMV surges as H1 earnings double.

text.p: Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV sent its shares surging on Tuesday by posting a 105 percent rise in half-year earnings and forecasting full-year profits before interest and tax of around five billion schillings ($390.1 million).

Austria's biggest industrial concern said cost-cuts, a robust performance from refining and marketing, its exploration & production (E&P) and plastics businesses pumped up earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) to 3.11 billion schillings from 1.52 billion.

Pre-tax profits in the first half jumped to 2.93 billion schillings from 1.56 billion but net profits were reined in by a hefty restructuring charge to cover the group's stringent job cut plans. They climbed to 1.35 schillings from 1.24 billion schillings.
"This dramatic profit growth is due to persistently good market conditions and a consistent focus on cost management," the company said in its results statement.

Chief executive Richard Schenz told a news conference that OMV plans to slash around 1,000 jobs by the end of 1998, leaving it with 7,500 staff. He also promised shareholders further cost-cuts to help reduce the group's cost base.

Schenz said the company, which hopes to make savings worth around one billion schillings per year after the restructuring programme is complete, was taking out a two billion schilling provision this year to cover severance and pension payments for around 600 job losses.

OMV -- which saw a strong dollar and a healthy demand for oil push up sales, excluding oil tax, to 45.31 billion schillings from 37.35 billion -- said net profits in the full year would be "at least slightly" above last year.
The company expects a Brent crude oil price of around $19 per barrel in the second half of 1997. On Tuesday, Brent was quoted at around $18.60 per barrel.

Although analysts had expected the company to outstrip most European rivals, one dubbed the figures "stunningly good" as OMV's shares surged 101.7 schillings to 1,756.5 in brisk trade, helping to lift Austria's blue-chip ATX index.

New volumes from OMV's international projects such as the Murzuk field in Libya, solid European demand for gas and a focus on streamlining OMV's Austrian filling stations in favour of expansion into high-growth neighbouring eastern European countries is expected to trigger above average earnings growth, analysts said.
Analysts said they were pencilling in higher earnings forecasts ahead of OMV's planned meeting in London on Wednesday.
"With a strong commitment to cost cutting and profitable volume growth, OMV will be well positioned to outperform," said London brokers Lehman Brothers in a note. ($ = 12.81 Austrian Schillings)
